cards.title: Create the cloud environment for the docs worker
cards.why: The docs worker cannot start without its environment. Epic wc-4 (the user guide) waits on it.
cards.context: One environment per worker profile. It holds the profile name as a variable and a setup script that installs the tools the checks need. Nothing secret goes in it: anyone who uses the environment can read its variables and script.
steps: Open claude.ai/code, then Settings → Cloud environments → Add cloud environment.
Environment variables: paste the first text below.
Setup script: paste the second text below, whole. Do not replace it with a line that runs a file from the repository.
Save, start a session in this environment, and paste the opening message the coordinator gives you.
Mark this card answered with the new session's URL in the note.

texts.label: Setup script
texts.text:
#!/bin/bash
# control-room: setup script for the docs profile. Paste whole.
set -u
log() { printf 'control-room setup: %s\n' "$*"; }
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	(apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq jq) || log "jq install failed"
fi
python3 -c 'import jsonschema' 2>/dev/null ||
	python3 -m pip install -q --break-system-packages jsonschema || log "jsonschema install failed"
(apt-get install -y -qq shellcheck bats || log "shellcheck/bats failed") &
wait
log "done for profile ${CR_PROFILE:-<unset>}"
exit 0

cards.source: coordinator: epic wc-4 is assigned to profile docs, which has no session

cards.title: How should wc count words in text that is not ASCII?
cards.why: Epic wc-3 (count words) is ready except for this; the worker counted ASCII only and asked.
cards.context: Today `wc` splits on ASCII spaces. Text with non-breaking spaces or in scripts without spaces (Chinese, Japanese) counts oddly. The fix is small either way; the choice is what users are promised.

choices.label: Split on every Unicode space
choices.consequence: Matches what most people expect for European text. Scripts without spaces still count as one word per run. One more test.

choices.label: Keep ASCII spaces only, and document it
choices.consequence: No code change. The README says what counts as a word.

choices.label: Use a word segmenter library
choices.consequence: Correct for every script, but the tool gains its first dependency.

links.label: The worker's question in the handoff

answer.note: Yes, and say in the README that scripts without spaces are not segmented.

cards.title: May the test fixtures include a paragraph of a published novel?
cards.why: The docs worker wants real prose in the examples. It stopped rather than guess about the licence.
cards.context: The paragraph would be about 80 words from a book still under copyright. A public-domain text works as well for the tests.

answer.note: No. Use the first paragraph of a public-domain text and name its source in the fixture.

cards.resolution: Relayed to the docs worker in its next brief; it used a public-domain paragraph and named the source. Landed with epic wc-2.
